visa-preparation.fastest_entry: No visa: Luxembourg is reached through Schengen (it's a member), so the Schengen 90 days in 180 rule applies in practice.
steps: Luxembourg has a bilateral visa waiver with Australia usable after the Schengen 90 days; tell the first border guard if you plan to use it.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES); it's free.
Stays over 90 days need a national visa or a bilateral waiver arranged before travel.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

The DAC (Directorate of Civil Aviation) registers operators through MyGuichet.lu, mainly those based in Luxembourg. EU/EASA residents register in their own country. Registration or renewal costs EUR 10 from 14 January 2026 (A$15.89 at EUR 0.6293 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026).
People living in a third country can email the DAC (uas@av.etat.lu) for how to register.

The DAC says only the UAS geographical zones shown on the Geoportail map at g-o.lu/uas are legally applicable; manufacturer geozones in a controller may not match. Red zones are active and need an authorisation request or notification. The data is also published as JSON at drones.geoportail.lu/zones.

items.text: Since 21 July 2023 an adult may grow up to four cannabis plants per household, from seed, at home, out of sight of the street, and adults may use and hold that cannabis at home (Law of 19 February 1973, arts 7-2).

Using cannabis anywhere else, or carrying, holding or buying up to 3 g in public, is an offence: police or customs can issue a EUR 145 fixed fine, or a court fine of EUR 25 to 500 (art 7-3). Visitors cannot lawfully buy cannabis.
Over 3 g: 8 days to 6 months' prison and/or EUR 251 to 2,500 (art 7-1(2)); using at work, at school or in front of minors carries the same range.

Using cannabis anywhere else, or carrying, holding or buying up to 3 g in public, is an offence: police or customs can issue a EUR 145 fixed fine, or a court fine of EUR 25 to 500 (art 7-3). Visitors cannot lawfully buy cannabis. Over 3 g: 8 days to 6 months' prison and/or EUR 251 to 2,500 (art 7-1(2)); using at work, at school or in front of minors carries the same range.

The DAC says only the zones on its Geoportail map (g-o.lu/uas) are legally applicable, and that geozones built into a drone's controller may not cover Luxembourg's restricted areas. Red zones are active and need an authorisation request or notification.
